x: Ferdinando, the new Mitcham star, quickly caught Tom Scrimshaw and then displayed poor tactics in endeavouring to take the lead. He did not succeed in this, and over the last sprint Scrimshaw went away and so gave us back our 20yds lead.
The Belgrave team went away from the rest of the field, in company with Coe, of St. George's, and Ferdinando, of Mitcham, and eventually finished in the following order : 1, W.
Ferdinando, of Mitcham, ran a good race to win in 4min. 46secs., and his team finished second, with Croydon just beating Epsom for third position.
Joe Flower, up against Norman Gunn, held his own but that was all, and so when Tom Scrimshaw went off for the final half he was about 40 yds. down on Ferdinando of Mitcham.

In the 4 x 880 yards, Tom Scrimshaw went first and broke Ferdinando's heart, Tom handing over at least 60 yards to the good. Frank and Bill Webb, running second and third, increased our lead and finally Jim Tosh lapped the Epsom man and ran out an easy winner in time which was good, considering the track.
Frank Webb had Ferdinando, of Mitcham, to contend with on the last stage and, as we rather expected, the Mitcham man eventually beat Frank by about 5 yards.
Ferdinando, of Mitcham, ran a well-judged last stage against Ford and beat our man in the last 100 yards, leaving us to be content with second place.
